title: Lenguas de Carnero en Costra (Mutton Tongues in Crust)
description: Prepared with mutton, broth, and white wine.
steps: Cook the tongues with a little broth, a glass of white wine, a bundle of parsley, onion, a bay leaf, a little thyme and basil, half a garlic head, two cloves, salt and large pepper
Let boil half an hour over low heat and pour Spanish sauce over them

For the crust, take a fireproof plate and pour on the bottom a filling the thickness of a finger, made with bread crumbs, a little butter or grated ham, two raw egg yolks, chopped parsley and onion, a little substantial broth or strained broth, a tablespoon of broth from the pot, salt and large pepper
Mix everything and pour into the plate, which will be placed over coals until the filling sticks
Then drain the butter from it and serve the tongues with their small broth on top of this crust

title: Lenguas de Cordero a la Parmesana (Lamb Tongues Parmesan Style)
description: Prepared with lamb, grated cheese, and sauce.
steps: Cook twelve lamb tongues as described in the previous recipe.

Sprinkle with a little melted butter.
Place in the oven or under a domed cover to brown.

title: Lenguas de Cordero Envueltas (Wrapped Lamb Tongues)
description: Prepared with lamb, mushrooms, and shallots.
steps: Cook a dozen lamb tongues in a pan after soaking in water and removing the ganyote.
Once cooked, remove the skins and place on a plate to drain, covering with a pot lid and plate to shape them uniformly.
When cool, divide in half lengthwise while keeping the two halves united, forming small costillas.
Prepare the filling by finely chopping twenty-four selected, clean mushrooms with parsley, shallots, salt, coarse pepper, and nutmeg.
Cook this filling in a pot with {{source-7}} and one glass of white wine until almost no broth remains.
Add a little grated breadcrumbs to the filling.
Spread thin slices of cooked and flattened pork loin on a napkin after soaking in warm water.
Place each tongue with its filling on the pork slices and wrap.
Ten minutes before serving, place on a grill to brown.
Arrange on a plate in the form of a crown and serve with tomato or pepper sauce.

title: Lenguas de Ternera Aprensadas (Pressed Veal Tongues)
description: Prepared with veal, saltpeter, and salt.
steps: Wash and scrape six tongues very well and place in the sun for two hours
Mix six pounds of salt with half a pound of saltpeter
Rub the tongues thoroughly with this mixture and place them in an appropriate vessel
Add the remaining salt and cover with cloth
Place a considerable weight on top to press the tongues and keep them in this state for eight days
On the ninth day, repeat the operation from the first day, omitting only the washing and sun-drying of the tongues
Add all remaining salt and press again for another eight days
After this time, remove from the press, dry, and place in a cool location where they will keep for a long time without spoiling

title: Lentejas (Lentils)
description: Prepared with lentils, tomato, and onion.
steps: Cook the lentils.
Once cooked, chop plenty of tomato, onion, and garlic.
Fry this mixture in butter and oil with some sliced huauchinangos fish until it browns well.
Add a tablespoon of vinegar and a little sugar.
Add some chopped celery to fry with the mixture.
Once the vinegar has reduced, add a wide chile soaked and ground with some peppercorns.
Let fry and then turn the lentils into it and let them season.

title: Licor de Toronjil (Lemon Balm Liqueur)
description: Prepared with lemon, alcohol or wine, and syrup.

ingredients.name: Six to eight drops of lemon balm essence

Let it rest one or two days
After this time, sweeten with very clarified simple syrup of high or low concentration according to preference
Color with cochineal to imitate the color of the lemon balm flower
Filter the liquor
Bottle it, giving it the name of 'Kiss of Melissa'

title: Lletes (Spiritual Soups)
description: A soup made with onion, bread, and sesame.
steps: Put some water to boil with a whole onion and five mint leaves
Once the onion is cooked, remove it and also remove the mint

Add one crumbled loaf of bread, {{source-9}}, sesame, walnuts, pine nuts, and pieces of candied citron
Leave on the fire until the soup is thick
Serve with dragées and ground cinnamon on top

title: Lomo a la Casera (Loin Homestyle)
description: Loin larded with bacon is marinated with lemon, onion and oil, then cooked in a greased paper wrapping. It is served with a wine-and-broth pan sauce containing carrots and onions.
steps: Lard the thickest part of the loin with bacon and spread on a platter
Place five or six pieces of lemon and as many slices of raw onion on top
Sprinkle generously with oil so the meat becomes well impregnated and the oil coats around it
Dust with salt and pepper
After a quarter hour turn the meat so it soaks on both sides and season again
Remove the meat from the marinade and wrap in paper greased with lard and tied with string tightly
Place in a pan to cook with the rest of the marinade
When the meat is almost completely cooked, remove the paper wrapper
Finish cooking on low heat
Remove the meat when completely cooked
Add to the pan half a cup of broth or water, half a glass of white wine, some carrots and some onions
When serving pour this sauce over the loin with the juice of a lemon

title: Lomo de Doña Tertea (Doña Tertea's Pork Loin)
description: Prepared with pork, garlic, and lard.
steps: Coat two pork loins with salt and let sit for two days, turning occasionally.
After two days, grind two large peeled garlic heads and mix with a little salt.
Coat the loins well with the garlic mixture, ensuring it penetrates well.
Cover generously with lard and place in the oven.
Cook for a little over one hour.

Optional: serve with the following sauce: In a little lard, add a handful of flour, but first add some chopped onion and parsley; once transparent, add the flour just until it is partially cooked; add a little water; just before serving, add an egg yolk diluted in a little vinegar and do not heat further with the egg as it will cook.

title: Lomo de Puerto a la Botonesa (Pork Loin in the Botonese Style)
description: Prepared with pork, vinegar, and lemon rind.
steps: Remove the fat covering the loin, leaving only a small layer.
Roll the meat and cover with sage branches, tying firmly with string.
Place the meat in vinegar for two or three days with some cloves and lemon rind.
Remove from vinegar and place in a pot with half of the vinegar it was soaked in, one cup of defatted broth, salt and pepper, one or two onions and some carrots cut into pieces.
Cook for two or three hours over brisk heat at first, then moderate.
Place on a platter and serve with the defatted cooking sauce.

title: Lomo de Ternera Frío (Cold Veal Loin)
description: Prepared with veal, vinegar, and salt.
steps: In the morning, prepare the loin after cleaning it, adding salt, pepper and vinegar, and keep it thus for the rest of the day
In the night, remove it and place it in a press, leaving it there until the following day
On that day, place it in a pan with moderate fire to parboil it there
When the meat is tender, remove it from the fire
Empty the pot into a dish, ensuring the loin finishes cooking over two fires
As the broth is consumed, add a little tomato and chopped parsley on top without stirring
When serving at the table, garnish with lettuce and fried toasts

title: Lomo Flamenco (Flemish Loin)
description: Prepared with ham, carrots, and cabbage.
steps: Lard the loin with thick strips of ham
Season with salt and pepper
Fry in butter
Turn to brown on both sides
Place between two fires in a pot for two or three hours
Separately cook carrots and cabbage with broth
When the meat is cooked, place on a platter, alternating around it pieces of carrot with pieces of cabbage
To the sauce remaining in the pot add a cup of broth and a glass of white wine
Bring to a boil for a moment
Pour the sauce over the meat and vegetables when serving

title: Lomos de Ternera Rellenos de Yerbas (Veal Loins Stuffed with Greens)
description: Prepared with veal, lettuce, and raisins.

ingredients.name: chard or lettuce, cooked and fried
ingredients.sourceText: chard or lettuce, cooked and fried

steps: Make pieces of meat from the veal loin to slice, and fill them with cooked and well-fried chard or lettuce, seasoned with spices and mixed with raisins, almonds, pine nuts, chopped hard-boiled eggs, and if desired, pieces of candied citron
After filling the loins, secure them with very clean twine and place them to cook in a pot until they become very tender
Then place them in a sauce made with roasted, ground tomato and fried in lard, with bread toasted in the same to turn it the color of cinnamon, very finely minced onion and parsley
When serving at the table, add a spoonful of oil to the sauce, and decorate the plate of loins with small chiles, olives and hard-boiled eggs cut into small pieces

title: Lomos en Adobo (Pork Loins in Adobo)
description: Prepared with pork, epazote, and garlic.
steps: Take a loin and slice it.
Add some dry epazote, spearmint and oregano.
Grind four garlic cloves, pepper, cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, Castilian vinegar and the corresponding salt.
Grind ancho chile and soaked mulato chile without toasting, and let infuse from one day to the next.
The following day, fry in lard.

title: Longaniza Habanera (Havana-style Longaniza)
description: Prepared with vinegar, garlic, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: pork meat from the loin or muscle
ingredients.sourceText: pork meat from the loin or muscle

steps: Prepare an adobo composed of vinegar, oregano, salt, ground pepper, crushed cilantro, chopped garlic, and four bay leaves
Add pork meat from the muscle or loin
Let it take on the flavor of the adobo well for about an hour and a half
Chop the meat into very small pieces
Place in intestines and tie as if eight finger-widths apart
This sausage is always served by frying the longanizas

Set aside a small portion, fry it in a pan to test its seasoning, and if it lacks salt or needs more spice, add what is necessary to the whole mass of sausage
After filling the intestines, place them to cook in a pot with two or three

title: Longanizas o Butifarras para Camino (Sausages for Travel)
description: Prepared with meat, pork or pork fat, and beef.

ingredients.name: One part pork loin or pork fat
ingredients.sourceText: One part pork loin or pork fat

steps: Mince two parts meat and one part pork loin or pork fat together
Season the mixture with salt and ground black pepper so that the pepper flavor predominates
After everything is well incorporated, let it rest for one or two hours
Fill the clean beef tripe with this mixture
Prick the tripe at intervals to allow air to escape
Tie with threads at distances of one-third of a vara, or leave them at the desired size for the sausages, with the thread hanging from both ends
Once all are filled, pass a stick or rope through their threads and place it over a pot with boiling water
Allow the sausages to cook suspended in the water without touching the bottom of the pot
When cooked, remove them on the same stick or rope they were placed on
Let them cool and hang them in the air where the sun does not reach them
Eat them cold, roasted, or fried in lard

ingredients.name: one and one half pounds of powdered sugar
ingredients.sourceText: one and one half pounds of powdered sugar

steps: Pound one and one half pounds of almonds and set to dry

Spread the paste on a wide flat spatula and form macarons the size of a small walnut
Bake in the oven at moderate heat like sponge cake, and glaze in the same manner

title: Macarrones de Almendras Amargas (Almond Macaroons with Bitter Almonds)
description: Prepared with bitter almonds, egg whites, and powdered sugar.
steps: Place 1 pound of bitter almonds on a clean cloth and rub them to remove dust
Grind them in a marble mortar with 4 egg whites, being careful not to grind them too much and to prevent them from turning into oil
Transfer the ground mixture to a bowl and incorporate 3 pounds of powdered sugar
If the paste is too dry, add egg whites, ensuring it is neither too liquid nor too thick
Arrange small portions the size of a walnut on sheets of paper
Bake the macaroons in the oven at a very gentle and steady heat

title: Magras Aragonesas (Aragonese Ham Slices)
description: Prepared with ham, lard, and garlic.

ingredients.name: ham of the best quality
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of ham of the best quality

steps: Take one pound of the best quality ham, wash it well and scrub it with a small brush
Scrape it with a knife so it releases all the red color
Cook it in a pot with water
Cut it into slices the size of a cigar
In a separate pot, heat oil and lard and fry garlic and onion with a little parsley until sautéed
Take large olives, chop them finely and fry them with capers
Take very ripe tomatoes, remove the seeds and chop them raw, add them to the pot and fry well
Grind clove and pepper and add to the mixture
When seasoned, add the ham slices and if more oil is needed, add it
Let it thicken
Garnish with large olives, capers, large capers, and fried bread

Scrape it with a knife so it releases all the red color
Cook it in a pot with water
Cut it into slices the size of a cigar
In a separate pot, heat oil and lard and fry garlic and onion with a little parsley until sautéed
Take large olives, chop them finely and fry them with capers
Take very ripe tomatoes, remove the seeds and chop them raw, add them to the pot and fry well
Grind clove and pepper and add to the mixture
When seasoned, add the ham slices and if more oil is needed, add it
Let it thicken
Garnish with large olives, capers, large capers, and fried bread

title: Magras de Jamón Rebanadas (Sliced Ham Magras)
description: Prepared with ham, garlic, and lard.
steps: Toast ham slices that are neither too thick nor too thin
Between two slices place cooked ham chopped very finely and finely chopped garlic
Heat a little water and lard in a pot and add more garlic
When the water is consumed, add onion chopped very finely, in quantity about one third of the ham
When cooked, add ground tomato without seeds, browned garlic and a little pepper
When seasoned, add the ham and for each half pound add two yolks of hard-boiled egg ground, which should be mixed from the metate with very little water
Incorporate this into the fried mixture with a little fresh chopped parsley, capers, chopped olives and a little oil
Let it thicken and serve

ingredients.name: A little lard for greasing the molds

steps: In a vessel without grease, beat eight eggs with half a pound of very finely ground sugar
When the egg is forced by hard beating, add half a pound of well-ground starch

Put in a well-tempered oven, and if you don't have one, use a pot placed on the fire with a comal on top

title: Manjar Blanco (French Fritters of Blancmange)
description: Prepared with cream, nuts, and flour.
steps: Dissolve in two cuartillos of cream, {{source-1}}, a little salt and a little lemon zest
Let the mixture cook for about three hours, stirring from time to time and after having covered the stove
When the blancmange is about to finish cooking, add sugar with four mazapanes and two crushed sweet pignolia nuts, and let it finish cooking
Incorporate three eggs one by one and make the paste bind together, which is spread on the cloth of a pan
Sprinkle with flour and let it cool
Divide into small square pieces and make small balls the size of grapes with them
At the moment of serving, heat butter in a pan, place in it the strainer, in which the fritters will have been placed, and shake the strainer frequently
As soon as the fritters have turned dark, remove them, let them drain, sprinkle them with sugar and serve
If desired, very finely chopped chicken breasts can be incorporated into the blancmange

Drain the rice, grind very well in a metate, strain through a sieve into a new earthenware bowl
Place in a cazo and add 30 cuartillos of milk strained through a cloth, previously sweetened with 7 pounds of very white sugar, coarsely ground

Add about 2 caldron cups of cold water and grains of well-washed salt
Place over high fire to boil vigorously, then add a little coarsely ground almond
Stir without removing from fire so it does not burn, and do not touch what sticks to the sides of the cazo until it is about to be poured into plates
Pour into dishes when a small amount placed on the back of a well-glazed ceramic plate comes off easily

title: Manjar-Blanco en Torteras para Casas de Comunidad (Blancmange in Molds for Community Houses)
description: Prepared with rice, corn, and lard.

ingredients.name: 1 whole chicken breast, cooked without salt
ingredients.sourceText: 1 whole chicken breast, cooked without salt

steps: Grind 8 pounds of rice; wash it well, place on a cloth in the sun, and when very dry, sift through a fine sieve until it becomes like powder
Place 4 cubos of milk in a cazo and mix 4 pounds of the sifted rice powder (accounting for weight loss from 8 pounds ground)
Take some prepared corn called nixtamal, and as soon as it begins to husk, place in a chiquihuite and wash very well
Place in the sun like the rice, and when dry, grind and sift in the same manner as the rice, doing both separately
Add 1 pound 6 ounces of this corn to the cazo with the rice, and 0.5 arroba of sugar
If the milk is very fatty, remove the cream and do not strain again; alternatively, set aside one cubo to dissolve the sugar and strain it for any debris, then combine everything

When it begins to thicken, add 4 ounces of lard and 1 whole chicken breast that has been cooked without salt and shredded finely (the chicken should be killed the day before and wrapped in a damp cloth to shred the breast)
Add the shredded chicken when the blancmange begins to boil
Once it has boiled well, test the point by inserting a knife and letting it cool; if it does not stick to the hand, it is ready
Remove from heat, and pour while not too hot because it will rise and overflow the molds
The molds should not be burned, but rather placed in the sun for 2 or 3 days after scrubbing

title: Manjar-Blanco Ordinario (Ordinary Almond Cream)
description: Prepared with rice, white sugar, and chicken breast.

ingredients.name: one pound and a half of clean rice
ingredients.sourceText: one pound and a half of clean rice

ingredients.name: four and a half pounds of white sugar
ingredients.sourceText: four and a half pounds of white sugar

steps: Weigh the clean rice, then wash it very well in a metate
Grind it so that no grains remain
Dissolve all of this in the milk, placed in a pan
Strain through a cloth into another pan, and a second time through finely woven fabric, taking care that all cloths used for this are well washed so the milk does not curdle
Rub the outside of the pan where it will cook with a well-ground garlic head, and do the same on the bottom to prevent burning
Put on the fire and stir constantly on all sides with force using a stick with a cloth so that the manjar does not stick
Have a cooked and ground chicken breast ready, dissolved in a little of the same milk, and add it a little before it reaches the point
If desired, one can use instead of the breast one pound of almonds, which are blanched, ground and added in the same manner as the breast, and it is more delicious with the almonds
When a spoonful placed on a plate, if when cold it pulls away leaving it clean, the manjar has reached a good point

title: Mantequilla Batida con Almíbar (Butter Whipped with Syrup)
description: Prepared with butter and syrup.
steps: Select fresh firm butter and clean it of all foreign matter
Put it in a pan with cold high thread syrup
Beat both together by hand, adding the syrup little by little and not all at once, in the quantity necessary for the butter to remain agreeably sweet
Continue beating with a spoon rather than by hand until it hardens well
Empty onto a moistened napkin prepared on a table
Place spoonfuls of the compound butter on the napkin, flattening and rounding them slightly with the spoon
Or extract with a pastry syringe, making letters or rings as the butter comes out
Leave on the table in a cool place, bringing out to the night air, frequently moistening the napkin so that water does not fall directly on the butter
Lift from the napkin with a knife and arrange on the serving platter in layers, decorated with cinnamon powder and dragée
Good for accompanying chocolate, but these butters melt easily and last little time if not kept in a cool place

title: Marasquino de Zara (Maraschino of Zara)
description: Prepared with brandy, cherries, and cherry.

ingredients.name: Three and a half jars of refined brandy
ingredients.sourceText: Three and a half jars of refined brandy

ingredients.name: Two and a quarter arrobas of sour cherries, well ripe
ingredients.sourceText: Two and a quarter arrobas of sour cherries, well ripe

ingredients.name: Eighteen pounds of refined and crushed sugar
ingredients.sourceText: Eighteen pounds of refined and crushed sugar

ingredients.name: orange blossom spirit
ingredients.sourceText: Six ounces of orange blossom spirit

ingredients.name: One and a half ounces of jasmine spirit
ingredients.sourceText: One and a half ounces of jasmine spirit

steps: Place in infusion in refined brandy two and a quarter arrobas of sour cherries, well ripe, in a hermetically sealed vessel, and leave for two or three days, then proceed to distillation in a water bath to obtain forty to forty-five cuartillos of spirituous liquor, according to the strength of the brandy used.

Then distill {{source-2}}, which will have been kept in sufficient quantity of water, to obtain after distillation forty-five to fifty cuartillos; in this distilled water dissolve eighteen pounds of refined and crushed sugar, and mix with the spirituous liquor obtained from the cherries, with one jar of kirchwasser, {{source-6}}, another {{source-7}} and one and a half ounces of jasmine spirit.

This liquor should have a taste and perfume of the most pleasant kind, and it is necessary to note that the jasmine spirit that should be used must be made with fresh oil, because when it has been kept a long time, it tends to be rancid, and in that case it imparts to the liquor a very acrid and disagreeable taste.

title: Marinada Cocida (Cooked Marinade)
description: Prepared with carrots, onions, and bay leaves.
steps: Place butter in a pot over the fire with three sliced carrots and four sliced onions, two bay leaves, a little thyme and two cloves

Add sprigs of parsley and some small bulb onions, which are also partially fried or macerated
Add two spoonfuls of flour and stir with the butter
Add one glass of vinegar and two glasses of broth with the corresponding salt and pepper
Let everything simmer over a gentle fire for about an hour
After that time, pass the marinade through a sieve to use as needed

title: Marquesote de Rosa (Rose Marquesote)
description: Prepared with syrup, egg whites, and lemon juice.
steps: Clarify the syrup and beat egg whites
For each pound of syrup add two egg whites and beat until very stiff
The syrup should be almost at the taffy stage
For each pound of sugar add the juice of one lemon, which is added when at the proper point, which is when dipping a finger in cold water it forms a thimble shape
Then remove from heat and add the rose and beat strongly with all your strength
Put in the mold and add grageé on top
The rose is added according to each person's taste

title: Masa Cocida para Marquesote a la Francesa (French Cooked Cake Batter)
description: A cake made with lemon rind, fruits or preserves, and water.
steps: Put water, butter, lemon rind, and salt in a saucepan
Heat the mixture until it begins to boil
Sift flour over the saucepan and add as much as it can absorb
When the batter becomes very thick, let it cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon
Allow to cool
Break eggs into it one at a time, mixing each thoroughly, adding more until the batter becomes soft
Grease a large saucepan with butter, sized so the batter fills only one quarter of its height initially, as it will fill completely when cooked
Place in a hotter oven than for ordinary cakes
The cake should be somewhat dry when done
Remove from the saucepan and coat the interior with diluted candied fruits or preserves

title: Masa de Armar Superior (Superior Building Dough)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, flour, and butter.
steps: Put two quarts of flour on a table and make a hole in the middle
Put there {{source-1}}, half an ounce of salt, six egg yolks, and one glass of water
Mix the butter with the eggs, salt, and water, and gradually mix in the flour, until all is combined
Knead the dough so that it hardens well, and add water if it is too dry

Lower or pound it twice, because if kneaded more, there would be the risk of burning it, especially in summer or in months of great heat, and then it would not hold together and would break when assembled

If you want to make a large quantity, three pounds of butter, two ounces of salt, and ten egg yolks are necessary for six pounds of flour, taking care in any case that the dough is very firm in order to avoid any inconvenience
If it is intended for cakes, make it more soft

title: Masa Hojaldrada (Puff Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with egg whites, flour, and salt.
steps: Place flour on a clean table forming a hole in the middle
Add salt, egg whites, water and butter to the hole
Gather the dough and let it rest for half an hour
Extend the dough with a rolling pin and cover with one pound of butter, well softened
If too warm, let rest again, then fold the two ends of the dough over the butter so it is well covered
Extend the dough with the rolling pin until it has only the thickness of a finger, fold in three layers and give four turns so what was at the side comes to the front
Roll the pin again - this is called one turn of dough
Repeat this operation as many times as necessary and let the dough rest until the oven is hot
Give two more turns before baking
Use as much butter as flour for five turns, and if there are three quarters butter to one part flour, six turns are needed

title: Masa para Empanadas ó Pasteles (Dough for Empanadas or Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with lard or butter, flour, and salt.

ingredients.name: five cuarterones of lard or good butter
ingredients.sourceText: five cuarterones of lard or good butter

steps: Put flour on a very clean board
Make a hole in the middle of the flour to put the lard in several portions and the salt
Add water judiciously and prudently, as too much would make the dough very soft and lacking consistency
Unite the lard with the water as well as possible
Little by little mix with the flour
Once the flour has absorbed all the water, knead well with force, it does not matter that this dough is very stiff as long as it is well sticky and contains no lumps
Make this dough at least two hours before using so it does not have time to rest and rise
With this dough, all kinds of empanadas are made, such as veal, rabbits, hares, poultry and fish

title: Masa Real (Royal Dough)
description: Prepared with water, butter, and sugar.
steps: Place water, fresh butter, sugar, finely chopped lemon zest, and salt in a pot or skillet
Put over fire, and when it begins to boil, move the skillet to the edge of the stove
Remove the lemon zest
Add flour little by little, as much as the water can absorb, stirring constantly and without ceasing
Place over fire for five minutes and remove when it reaches the right point, which will be known when the dough pulls away from the skillet
Then empty it into a cold earthenware vessel, adding one or two eggs until the dough sticks between your fingers

description: Prepared with egg yolk, juice, and olive oil.
steps: Place one raw egg yolk in a small bowl with a little salt and the juice of one lemon
Stir and turn continuously with a wooden spoon
Add oil in a thin stream while stirring
Add a little vinegar as the sauce thickens or curdles
Continue adding oil in this manner until a quarter liter is absorbed, taking care to add sufficient salt
Serve white, left as it naturally becomes after the above steps, or serve green by adding spinach green (see spinach green, page 322)
This sauce is used for cold fish appetizers or for salads of legumes cooked in salted water
It can also be made to curdle or congeal with snow or with calf brains in place of the raw yolk

title: Mayonesa Alternativa (Alternative Mayonnaise)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, vinegar, and lettuce.

ingredients.name: Three or four drops of edible oil
ingredients.sourceText: Three or four drops of edible oil

steps: Place two egg yolks in a pot with a little powdered salt and beat well with a clean and dry wooden spoon.
Add three or four drops of edible oil and continue beating.
Continue adding oil in this manner until it falls in a stream.
Crush one clove of garlic, add it, and continue beating until the oil is incorporated with the egg.
Add {{source-4}}, beat again, and add more oil.
These operations must be done without stopping beating, as the sauce breaks very easily.
When it is like a purée, it is done.
Finely chop a little lettuce and prepare it like a salad, adding a little powdered pepper; form it in the bowl like a cone.
Once the fish or chicken is prepared, cooked, and deboned, place the lettuce mixture on top to cover the piece and above it the prepared sauce, to which slices of boiled egg are usually added.

title: Mayonesa Blanca a la L.—E. A. (White L.—E. A. Mayonnaise)
description: Prepared with egg yolk, vinegar, and olive oil.
steps: Place one egg yolk, pepper, salt and a few drops of vinegar in a small bowl
Stir, turn and mix everything well
Add one tablespoon of olive oil drop by drop without ceasing to stir
Once the sauce is curdled and in sufficient quantity, add vinegar gently without stopping to turn the sauce
This is very delicate but patience is necessary as it takes a quarter hour or more to be well made and well turned
It serves to cover all kinds of cold birds and can be made green by adding parsley or tarragon when adding the eggs
If made by placing the bowl on crushed snow, it takes a more convenient consistency

title: Mayonesa con Lechuga Picada (Mayonnaise with Chopped Lettuce)
description: Prepared with lettuce, egg yolks, and olive oil.

ingredients.name: half a quarter liter of golden olive oil
ingredients.sourceText: half a quarter liter of golden olive oil

steps: Chop a little lettuce as for a salad and let it drain
Beat twelve egg yolks and while beating incorporate half a quarter liter of golden colored olive oil, not green
From time to time sprinkle with a little vinegar, continuing to beat until it curdles like custard
Season the sauce with the corresponding salt
Arrange on plates as follows: place a bed of mayonnaise on a platter, another of chopped lettuce and on top place the birds or fish already prepared
If the fish are white, they need only be boiled in water, and removing them without breaking, dry them well with a napkin and place them on the bed of chopped lettuce
Cover with mayonnaise and arrange the beds in this order as desired, the last always being egg

title: Mazapanes (Almond Paste Candies)
description: A confection made with almonds, egg whites, and wafers.
steps: Grind {{source-0}} on a metate, wetting it with one or two beaten egg whites so it does not become oily
Clarify {{source-2}} until it reaches hard-ball stage
Add the ground almonds to the clarified sugar
When the mixture pulls away from the pot, set it aside until the next day
Form small balls with wet hands and place them on wafers
Flatten slightly and make a cross in the center with a knife dipped in water
Send to the oven

For glazed mazapanes: clarify honey until it reaches a high hard-ball stage, scrape in green lemon zest, dip the mazapanes in and out of the honey, and dry on a platter while rolling them in powdered sugar

title: Mazapanes (Marzipan)
description: Prepared with ground almonds and sugar.
steps: Boil the sugar giving it the point of hard crack
Mix the almonds with the syrup and put on the fire until it reaches the point when tested by hand with water, and if it no longer sticks, it is ready
Remove from the fire and with wet hand make small balls
Score them like chocolate and place on wafers

title: Mazapanes Blando de Almendras Dulces y Amargas (Soft Sweet and Bitter Almond Marzipan)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, bitter almonds, and egg white.
steps: Soak 3 pounds of sweet almonds and 1 pound of bitter almonds, peel them and put them to dry
Crush them in a mortar, grinding them well so that they form a very fine paste, adding egg white from time to time
Make a sugar syrup with 3 pounds of the best sugar, clarify it and let it boil until it reaches the low ball point
Remove the pan from the fire and pour the almond paste into the syrup

Place the pan on embers and stir constantly so that it does not burn or stick, knowing that the paste is well made if when a little is placed on the back of your hand it can be removed without sticking
Pour onto a sugar-dusted table, let it cool and extend to the thickness desired, cutting it immediately into different shapes made with molds or tin cutters
Place on paper sheets and bake at moderate heat after glazing with sugar like biscuits

title: Mazapanes de Almendra Dulce (Sweet Almond Marzipan)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, egg white, and sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: clarified sugar syrup at flowering point
ingredients.sourceText: 1.5 pounds clarified sugar syrup at flowering point

steps: Blanch the sweet almonds in hot water
Dry them in a sieve after wiping well with a cloth
Grind them in a metate, adding egg white from time to time to prevent them from releasing oil
Once well ground, put this paste in 1.5 pounds of clarified sugar syrup at flowering point and stir well with a wooden spoon, taking care that it does not stick to the bottom of the pan
Know that the mass is at the right point if, touching it quickly with the back of your hand and lifting it promptly, nothing sticks to it
Place the paste on a tinned copper plate and dust with sugar all over, letting it rest until it cools
Put it on a clean board, cut with molds of the desired shape and form, transfer the cut pieces to paper placing them carefully
Bake at a moderate heat, and when cooked on one side, turn them over so they cook equally on both sides

title: Mazapanes Reales (Royal Marzipan)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, orange, and powdered sugar.
steps: Blanch 1 pound of sweet almonds, placing them in cold water as they are blanched
After draining them, grind them in a marble mortar, rolling them little by little with common water and a little orange blossom water
When well ground, put them in a pan with 1.5 pounds of powdered sugar and put them to dry over a small heat with a gentle fire
When applying your finger to the paste nothing sticks, remove from the heat and let it cool on a plate dusted with sugar
When cold, cut into small pieces, which are rolled and rounded, leaving them the thickness of a little finger, giving them all if possible the same volume
Then cut them to form with them a ring in the shape of a rosette
Line them on an iron grill, which will have been placed in a basin
Make a base or ring with the same paste, spread over it a light layer of apricot jam or other preserves, and cover the base or ring with the same marzipan paste, cut in the desired shape
Place on the grill, glaze with very white sugar and let it drain
Thread the marzipans on paper sheets and put them in the oven, somewhat lively so that they take color

title: Melspeiz de Col a la Polaca (Polish-Style Cabbage Melspeiz)
description: Prepared with cabbage, melted butter, and flour.
steps: Make a thick dough with two handfuls of flour, water, two eggs, a little melted butter and salt, and let it rest
Blanch two cabbage heads in boiling water, chop them very finely and cook with pepper and salt
Let cool and mix with five eggs, two tablespoons of curdled milk and a little nutmeg
Spread the dough very thin and wide, arrange the small piles of chopped cabbage on it, and fold the dough covering the filling
Cut the dough around each pile of cabbage in a way that small pieces like sacks or French toasts are formed

ingredients.name: half a pound of clarified syrup at the soft-ball stage, slightly warm
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of clarified syrup at the soft-ball stage, slightly warm

steps: Beat six fresh egg whites well.
Add them little by little to half a pound of clarified syrup at the soft-ball stage and slightly warm, with lemon or orange zest.
Stir everything constantly until the mixture reaches the proper consistency, which is known when a spoonful dropped onto itself stays on top without incorporating.
Distribute the meringues as desired on papers and dust with sifted sugar.
Place them in a bell-shaped oven with fire below and above, neither too strong nor too slow, and bake until they turn golden.
After baking, let them rest, then join each two meringues together, filling them with nougat foam.

title: Mermelada Superior de Membrillo (Superior Quince Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with quinces, orange, and sugar.
steps: Divide quinces into quarters and remove the cores
Cook with their skin in water until well cooked
Pass through a sieve and weigh the quantity
Cook the cores separately in a little water
Mix one part of the resulting jelly with the quince
Make a syrup with sugar in proportion of one and a half pounds for each pound of quince

Add the cooked quince, beating constantly in one direction only
Continue beating for a long time until the preserve feels heavy
Empty into molds
Alternatively, it can be made very white with raw quince, grated in water so it does not take color
Once drained, add to syrup that is left to boil until set, mixing in a little orange blossom water when removing from heat

title: Miel (Clarificación de la) (Honey Clarification)
description: Prepared with honey, lemons, and water.

ingredients.name: white Spanish chalk, finely ground
ingredients.sourceText: five pounds of white Spanish chalk, finely ground

ingredients.name: two and a half pounds of clarifying charcoal
ingredients.sourceText: two and a half pounds of clarifying charcoal

steps: Put the honey with eighteen cuartillos of water in a pot that can hold two arrobas
Dissolve the honey over fire
When dissolved, add five pounds of finely ground white Spanish chalk with the peels of three lemons
Stir carefully with a skimming spoon so it does not stick to the bottom of the pot
After some time, add two and a half pounds of clarifying charcoal and continue stirring
When the honey is about to boil, sprinkle it with a mixture of six beaten eggs and eighteen cuartillos of water until it resembles a sponge
Pass it through a cloth strainer as many times as necessary to give it proper clarity
Wash and drain the cloth one or two days before clarifying more honey, using a mixture of three eggs and water until it reaches ten degrees

title: Mole de Guajolotes (Turkey Mole)
description: Prepared with turkey, chile, and lard.
steps: Devein all the chiles and place lard in a skillet over low heat so the chile browns little by little
Grind tomatoes according to the quantity of chile and grind well
Toast a cuartilla of sesame seeds on the comal and grind dry until it yields; brown a real of almonds in lard and grind also dry with shells and combine with the sesame
Cut the turkey into quarters, wash it, dry with a cloth, and brown the portions in lard until golden
The day before, cook a pork knuckle with pork meat scraps and remove from heat when half-cooked
The next morning early, place the turkey in a clay pot
When ready to make the mole, heat water in a pot until very hot then lower heat

Place an empty clay pot on the fire and once hot add a little lard; when well hot add the chile to fry well, adding hot water little by little and breaking it up with a spoon; once well fried transfer to the pot with the turkey
In the same manner fry the tomato, break it up with a spoon in hot water and add to the pot with the turkey
Rinse the pot where the chile was fried with hot water where the turkey is cooking; brown the knuckle and scraps with all the broth in which it cooked
Place on the fire with everything together and add water in regular quantity but not so it becomes watery, adding it hot
Grind the almonds with a spoon and add to the mole
Toast some chile seeds and a little anise on the comal, taking care not to burn them

steps: Blanch and refresh the sweetbreads as described in previous articles.

Serve over chicory, cardoon, or tomato substrate, choosing whichever seems best.

Roast two or three heads of garlic and grind with cumin, clove, and pepper (each ground separately and dry)
Chop little parsley very finely
Chop six regular tomatoes finely
Chop less than one cup of tomatoes the same way
Remove mint leaves
Toast and break into pieces six wide chiles
Chop the fat from the tripe finely, yielding about one and a half cups
Mix everything with the blood and taste
Add whatever is lacking and let infuse for two hours
After washing the intestines, fill them, leaving space empty so they are not too crowded

title: Morcillas á la Francesa (French-Style Blood Sausages)
description: Prepared with onions, lard, and cream.

ingredients.name: lard per half azumbre of blood
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of lard per half azumbre of blood

steps: Cut onions into pieces and pass through melted lard without browning.
Mix with {{source-2}}, combining everything and adding finely chopped herbs, salt, spices, and cream.
With this mixture fill the intestines, having previously cleaned them well through a funnel.
Tie at one end and fill before tying, taking care not to make the tie too tight.
Cook in warm water until no blood comes out when pricked with a pin.
Then remove and let drain and dry, cutting pieces of varying lengths.
Note that the water should not boil as they would burst.
Place on grills or on a spit.

title: Morcones con Arroz Muy Buenos (Blood Sausages with Rice, Very Good)
description: Prepared with rice, pork, and chiles.
steps: Receive the pig's blood in a suitable bowl with a little salt, stirring by hand at the same time until it cools so it remains liquid and clean without straining
Wash {{source-2}}, tie it in a cloth napkin, and hang it inside a pot with water so that the rice bundle does not touch the bottom
Let it boil until the rice is half-cooked, then remove and let it drain
Devein and toast six broad chiles, then grind them until they become fine powder
Do the same with a little ginger, black pepper, and caraway
Chop a good amount of onion very finely in the raw state
Blanch it in a small basket or strainer by pouring boiling water over it so it passes through to the other side, leaving the onion blanched
Also chop the pork mesentery and diaphragm
Once everything is prepared with the necessary anticipation, mix it with the already cool blood, seasoning with the corresponding salt
With this mixture fill the thick pork intestines that have been well cleaned without removing the fat
Tie to leave the sausages the size desired and place to cook in boiling water
Eat them fried or grilled with a good chile sauce, or with another appropriate sauce if wine is to be drunk over them

title: Morones (Sweet Almond and Lard Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with lard, sesame seeds, and sugar.
steps: Take one pound of fresh lard and knead it with one pound of ground sugar and one pound of flour, adding a little salt.
Knead with the hands until the dough has no lumps or rough spots, and when it is smooth, divide it into equal quantities.
To one portion add one quarter ounce of ground cinnamon and mix well, then spread on paper to a thickness of one finger's width.
Sprinkle sesame seeds on top, then place the other portion of dough on top and sprinkle more sesame seeds over it.
Place between two comales (griddles) to cook, and when half-cooked, make cuts with a knife so the heat penetrates and it cooks well.
When cooked, break into small pieces, wrap in paper, and serve.

title: Mostachones a la Española (Spanish-Style Mostachones)
description: Prepared with almonds, citron or lemon, and syrup.

ingredients.name: pieces of candied citron or lemon
ingredients.sourceText: pieces of candied citron or lemon

ingredients.name: clarified syrup cooked to the crack stage
ingredients.sourceText: one pound clarified syrup cooked to the crack stage

ingredients.name: cinnamon and syrup for the glaze
ingredients.sourceText: cinnamon and syrup for the glaze

steps: Grind two pounds of almonds with their skin, sprinkling the mass from time to time with a little water to prevent it from turning to oil.
Place it then in a pot over low fire to dry, and add half an ounce of cinnamon passed through a drum sieve, a little fragrant water, and some pieces of candied citron or lemon.
When everything is dry, gradually add and mix one pound of clarified syrup cooked to the crack stage, little by little with a spoon, stirring the paste constantly so it does not stick to the pot.
When the dough is manageable, that is, when it does not stick to the hand, remove from the fire and empty it onto a plate to cool.
Then form the mostachones as described in the previous article (oval shape, pointed at the ends, four or five fingers long and three fingers wide).
These mostachones can be glazed, although many neither glaze nor bake them, as either way they are very good.
If you want them glazed, mix a little cinnamon with syrup and let it cook until it reaches the crack stage.
Then glaze the mostachones one by one, place them on paper, and set the glaze with the oven door cover.
